identity.title: Emergence of high-mass stars in complex fiber networks (EMERGE): IV. Environmental dependence of the fiber widths

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper, we have made use of the EMERGE Early ALMA Survey, a statistically significant sample of seven low- (NGC 2023, OMC-4 South), intermediate- (OMC-2, OMC-3, LDN 1641N), and high-mass (OMC-1, Flame Nebula) star-forming regions

question.value: How do fiber widths (FWHM) vary across different star-forming environments in Orion, and do they depend on peak column density and external pressure?

evidence.quote: Here, we aim to characterise the variation in the fiber widths under the different conditions explored by this survey.

method.value: Modified FilChap samples column density map perpendicular to fiber axis, averages the profile, fits Gaussian (also Plummer p=2, 4 for tests); temperature sampled along same cuts without averaging

evidence.quote: The column density map is sampled to determine the average density profile along the axis of each structure, which is then fitted with different orthogonal cuts

key_parameters.value: avg_len = 1, n2 = 2, npix = 45 and 43, dist_normal = 3 x theta_beam, order = 3

evidence.loc: Appendix: Changes to the public version
evidence.quote: We therefore set `avg`$\_$`len` = 1 and `n2` = 2 to have the radial sampling performed only around these points;

evidence.loc: Appendix: Changes to the public version
evidence.quote: obtaining $\sigma\sim3\times10^{21}$ cm$^{-2}$ for a typical temperature of 20 K seen across our fields.

assumptions.value: No baseline subtraction since column density floor term removed

evidence.quote: we avoid any baseline subtraction, usually applied by FilChap, since we removed the column density floor term

fitting.value: Gaussian chosen over Plummer: fewest unresolved widths, lowest reduced chi2, fewest free parameters (3 vs 4)

evidence.quote: it has the lowest degeneracy given the lower number of free parameters (3) compared to the Plummer profile (4)

validation.value: Compared Gaussian and Plummer fits via skewness, kurtosis, peak counts, reduced chi2, resolved fraction

evidence.quote: Figure [11] shows the reduced $\chi^2$ calculated for each cut as additional quality assessment for the fit.

method.value: Gradient = (T_bg - T_K^0)/Δx with Δx = ±0.1 pc from column density peak

evidence.quote: we chose a radial distance of $\pm0.1$ pc from the column density peak as representative of the environment outside the fiber.

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction of cuts with FWHM > 0.1 pc

evidence.quote: only 4% of our cuts show a $FWHM$ above 0.1 pc

findings_qualitative.value: Fiber widths vary systematically between regions; narrowest in OMC-1, OMC-2 and Flame Nebula, broadest in NGC 2023 and LDN 1641N

evidence.loc: 4 Environmental variation in the fiber widths
evidence.quote: Regions such as OMC-1, OMC-2, and the Flame Nebula have the narrowest individual cuts, with a median value of $\sim0.03-0.04$ pc.

claims.hypothesis: Fibers share a characteristic width of ~0.1 pc
claims.experiment: Gaussian fits of 991 radial cuts across 7 Orion regions
claims.result: Median FWHM 0.05 pc; only 4% of cuts above 0.1 pc
claims.finding: Fibers are narrower than 0.1 pc and no unique characteristic width exists

evidence.quote: this $FWHM$ is a factor of 2 lower than the previously proposed characteristic $\sim$ 0.1 pc width for parsec-scale filaments

claims.result: Median FWHM ranges 0.034 to 0.074 pc between regions

evidence.loc: 4 Environmental variation in the fiber widths
evidence.quote: We additionally observe a systematic variation in the fiber widths from region to region in our survey.

claims.hypothesis: FWHM anti-correlates with N0 above ~1e22 cm^-2 as predicted by models
claims.experiment: Compare fiber and HGBS FWHM-N0 with Fischera & Martin and Heitsch models
claims.result: Width drops with N0 above ~4e22 cm^-2
claims.finding: Anti-correlation observed, though models cannot fully fit

evidence.quote: While none of these models can fully constrain the observations

claims.result: Median gradient ~80 K/pc, >30 K/pc in most cuts

evidence.quote: all regions have the majority of cuts with temperature gradients $> 30$ K pc$^{-1}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Plummer fits with p=2 and p=4 rejected in favour of Gaussian

evidence.quote: Based on the previous tests, the Plummer ($p=2$) function appears as the worst choice to fit the radial profiles of the Orion fibers.

limitations_admitted.value: Model applicability limited: fibers are non-isothermal prolate spheroids; pressure estimates assume equilibrium

evidence.quote: the above first-order calculations assume an equilibrium solution for these objects.
